answer: Yes, strongly biased low. Across 167 MODZCTA areas with >=20 structural fires in 2025 (valid records, travel time not response time), the model's median nearest-firehouse drive time is 1.53 min versus FDNY's recorded median travel of 3.85 min. The model underestimates by 2.23 min on average (95% bootstrap CI 2.14-2.31); observed is about 2.4x modeled. Incident-weighted bias is 2.16 min. It under-predicts in 100% of areas, only 3% fall within 1 min, and correlation is weak (r=0.48), so the shortfall is not a constant offset: it is proportionally worst where the model is fastest (Manhattan 2.6 min, Bronx 2.5, Queens 2.2, Staten Island 2.1, Brooklyn 1.7). This is a lower bound on travel time (posted speed, no traffic/signals/turns, point-to-point), so the direction is expected; the cause is not isolated here.
traps_or_caveats: Used travel time (incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy), not response time; comparing to response (adds turnout) would inflate bias to 2.95 min.
Used only valid_incident_rspns_time_indc='Y', structural fires, 2025 only; the finding applies to that incident type/year.
Areas with <20 incidents excluded and listed (10 areas: 10004, 10005, 10006, 10044, 10069, 10280, 10282, 10464, 11109, 11697); including them barely changes the result (2.27 min).

ZIP geography: observed rows are postal ZIPs mapped to MODZCTA. The case code's zcta-list mapping drops ZIP 11249 (94 fires) though the MODZCTA label places it in 11211; I mapped it via the label. Still unmatched and not scored: 10151 (1), 10178 (1) and 110 fires with a null ZIP.

Model is a deliberately optimistic lower bound: posted speed with no traffic, signals, turns, intersection delay or acceleration; ~12,000 segments use default speeds (25 mph for ordinary streets) when posted_speed is missing; origins/destinations snapped to the network within 500 ft; 540 of 103,215 street points not reached within the 15-min cutoff (truncates long times, negligible).

Model gives each street-segment midpoint equal weight, while real fires are not uniformly distributed over segments; and observed is the first-arriving unit, which may not be the nearest firehouse. Neither explains a ~2.2 min one-signed offset, but they limit area-level accuracy.

I did not decompose the bias into causes (congestion vs. turnout-excluded dispatch/dismount vs. speed assumptions); that would need unit-level data or a sensitivity run. Medians of ZIP medians are combined incident-weighted across postal ZIPs (approximation, not a true area median).

Network and street points reused from cached C:\proveit_work\fire_ems.gdb (copied to T11_work.gdb); the model was not rebuilt. Score My Layer was not used since the comparison is area-level and computed directly.
